lessons.title: Practice Views Indexes
lessons.description: Create a view active_users that selects username and email from users where role is not guest. Also create an index on users(email). The test checks that the view returns at least 4 rows.
lessons.starter_code:
-- TODO: create view active_users (username, email of non-guests) and an index on users(email)
SELECT username, email FROM users WHERE 0;

source.name: SQLite official documentation (sqlite.org) — CREATE VIEW — 'assigns a name to a pre-packaged SELECT statement'

learning_objectives: Quarry clerks recount crates before dawn, and store a query as a reusable view with CREATE VIEW.

exercises.question: Quarry clerks recount crates before dawn, and store a query as a reusable view with CREATE VIEW.
hints: Read the one job this step is practicing.
The example is about Views Indexes.
CREATE VIEW kitchen AS SELECT name FROM products

exercises.question: Quarry clerks recount crates before dawn. For store a query as a reusable view with CREATE VIEW, which line reads names through a view?
hints: Compare each line with the example.
One line matches the example.
CREATE VIEW kitchen AS SELECT name FROM products
exercises.explanation: CREATE VIEW stores the select, and reading the view runs it.
options: CREATE VIEW kitchen AS SELECT name FROM products

exercises.question: Quarry clerks recount crates before dawn. For store a query as a reusable view with CREATE VIEW, what value is displayed?
hints: Run the example in your head from the top.
The last line is what gets displayed.
exercises.explanation: The Views Indexes program displays that value.
exercises.starter_code:
CREATE VIEW kitchen AS SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Kitchen';
SELECT name FROM kitchen;

exercises.question: Quarry clerks recount crates before dawn. For store a query as a reusable view with CREATE VIEW, what does the second run display?
